label: model-proved
statement: If Store.append o vs succeeds, every location that was readable is still readable, and every readable location that is neither the grown array nor an ancestor of it reads the same value. Typed form: if o has type grow E and the new elements have type E, every typed location stays typed, o stays grow E, the new elements are read at o++[n+i], and the store refines the old one.
differs_from_target: The target 'read (push s o v) l = read s l' is false for the grown array and its ancestors, whose content is the array, so those are excluded; the statement is about Store.append (the operation eval uses), not a separate push. Val.resizable now records its element type so that growing an empty array cannot change which array type it has.
assumptions: Typed form assumes the elements have the element type.
witnesses: sampled_extent golden: reference to element 0 read after a push; forms1 growing loop

label: model-proved
statement: validate m = ok -> for every fuel and profile, each of the fourteen evaluation functions, run on code of m from a state satisfying the frame invariant, does not fault and ends in a state satisfying it (Specs). The frame invariant contains the store invariant StoreInv: every reference or slice any root holds denotes a typed location or a run inside a typed array, and points into a root that ends no earlier than its holder. Scope exit is the block component: after execBlock releases its scope instance the frame of the surrounding code holds, because every surviving root is older than the instance and so holds no reference into it. Corollary: a run of an accepted module that ends leaves LiveRefs true of the final store.
differs_from_target: The invariant is stated over the whole store, not over a demand set (the pilot profile has no shrink, so every stored reference must stay valid). During the initialization of global g a reference to a later global may exist and be passed, but not used: the invariant there allows a reference to the whole of a global not yet bound (Unbound), and LiveRefs in the earlier sense holds once all globals are bound. The per-function statements take the validator's own results for the code as hypotheses (tyExpr = ok, rpExpr = ok); the statement free of checker functions is TH-CORE-01.
witnesses: rejected_root_forged_annotation, rejected_result_local, rejected_block_value_dangling and rejected_call_param_assumption each break the invariant at a block exit or a call and fault with dangling_root under --no-validate

label: model-proved
theorem: Goose.Proofs.Safety.validated_context_sound; per-item facts Goose.Core.Sound.validate_modOk; entry shape Goose.Proofs.Core.th_core_01_entry
statement: validate m = ok -> for every context c of m, every fuel, profile and call depth, every store s satisfying StoreInv with all globals bound, and every argument list of the parameters' types whose references point into roots P gives each parameter (roots older than the call) and into the context's annotation of that parameter: enterCall does not fault, and if it returns then StoreInv holds again, every typed location is still typed, every reference stored before the call is unchanged, no root was added, and the result has the result type and points only into the roots the context declares for the result, read through P.
differs_from_target: The target names a predicate WellFormed that is the conjunction of the validation rules as propositions. No declarative typing or root judgment was written: the checker functions remain the only statement of the rules, and what acceptance is shown to give is this semantic property of every context, stated over stores, values, locations and the module's own annotations. It is the fundamental lemma of a logical relation, not a syntactic well-formedness judgment.
assumptions: validate m = ok. The hypotheses on s, the arguments and P are the precondition of the semantic property, discharged by the caller's own check at every call the evaluator makes and trivially at the entry.
witnesses: INDEX fixtures for each rule; the entry call of every golden and example module is an instance

label: model-proved
evidence: For modules m, m' with equal implementation tables, globals and entry, and contexts that name the same implementation at every index, eval n p m = eval n p m' for every fuel n and numeric profile p. The erased fields are every Context field other than impl: decl, varRoots, resultRoots. eval_eraseRoots instantiates it with a module whose contexts have no declaration key and no roots.
limits: The target says replacing a module's context table changes no result; proved: replacing it while keeping each context's implementation index and the entry. A different implementation index is a different program (TH-SHARE-01 covers the case where it is justified). files, types and origins are not constrained because eval reads none of them; origins are read only by the tool when it prints a line number.
assumptions: None beyond the Core definitions of eval.
witnesses: Goose/Share/Examples.lean: the first golden with its root annotations erased is rejected by validate and runs to the same output.

label: model-proved
evidence: If Quotient m m' q rho holds then eval n p m = eval n p m' for every n and p. Quotient: header tables, entry and globals of m' equal those of m; m' has the contexts of m at the same indices with impl mapped by q; every implementation f a context of m names is, in m, the body m' holds at q f with its callees renamed by rho f; rho f sends each context to one that m' maps to the same implementation. The proof is a simulation by induction on fuel over the evaluator's mutual definitions, so mutually recursive groups need no separate argument.
limits: Differs from the target in three ways. (1) Bodies name contexts, not implementations, so the renaming that makes two bodies equal acts on context indices (rename by rho f, chosen per implementation: identity or a representative map) instead of one map q on implementation indices; q maps only the implementation index of each context. (2) Nothing is demanded of implementations no context names, which a run cannot reach; quotient_of_implwise gives the plan's every-implementation form when every context names an existing one. (3) Globals, files, types and origins must be equal (no merging of global initializers).
assumptions: None beyond the Core definitions of eval.
witnesses: test/semantics/share/INDEX (checked by run_index.sh) and Goose/Share/Examples.lean: issue-9 shape, free variable bound to two locals, mutually recursive pair, merge after one round; counterexamples: bodies differing in one operation and callees that differ stay distinct, forged merges are rejected, and the forged modules behave differently.

feature: a quotient of a never-faulting module never faults
label: model-proved
evidence: If Quotient m m' q rho and eval n p m is never a fault, then eval n p m' is never a fault. share_validated_never_faults takes the safety statement (validate m = ok implies no fault at any fuel and profile) as an explicit hypothesis and concludes the same for a validated m.
limits: The safety theorem is a hypothesis, not an import: this row says nothing until TH-SAFE-01 is proved for the same eval. The quotient m' is not claimed to validate: renaming callee contexts in a merged body can name a context whose annotations do not suit every caller context.
witnesses: Goose/Share/Examples.lean: the proposals of the fixtures validate and run to the unshared output.

label: model-proved
evidence: checkQuotient m m' qt rt = true implies Quotient m m' (fun f => qt.getD f f) (bodyRenaming m m' _ rt). The witnesses qt and rt are untrusted: a wrong one makes the check fail.
limits: Soundness only. Completeness (every quotient has witnesses the checker accepts) is not proved; goose-semantics share rebuilds the witnesses from the context tables and accepts the proposer's output and the fixtures. Bodies are compared with the implementation name, variable names and summary, so functions that differ only in a name are not merged.
witnesses: test/semantics/share/INDEX: three forged claims rejected, proposals accepted.

label: executable

label: model-proved
theorem: Goose.Reuse.cachedRun_result, cachedRun_consistent, cachedRuns_agree, cachedRuns_agree_from, cachedRun₂_result, cachedRuns₂_agree
evidence: If the key determines the result and the cache is consistent, cachedRun returns the uncached result and leaves the cache consistent; any sequence of cached runs from the empty cache (or any consistent cache) returns the uncached results; two stages in a row, the second keyed on the first's result, have the same property.
limits: A cache is an association list (entries are only added for absent keys). The model is independent of Core and says nothing about any real stage.
assumptions: KeyDetermines: key i = key j implies run i = run j, which is the completeness of dependency tracking. Assumed, not proved; see the next row.

label: model-proved
statement: moduleA m = true -> eval n p m = done o t -> exists k, GIR.run k p (lower m) = done o t, for every Core module m, numeric profile p, fuel n, outcome o and output t.
differs_from_target: Only the fragment moduleA, a decidable predicate: every global initializer and the entry function's body use only these forms - expressions lit, bool, read, ref, slice, len, un, bin, cmp, not, conv, push, arrLit, fill; places var, global, deref, elem; views of and val; bounds; statements let, assign, assign-op, rebind, expr, append, print; and the entry takes no parameter. Excluded: and, or, if-expressions, block expressions, calls; if, while, for-range, for-each, return, break, continue, assert, abort and exit statements. Nothing about faults: a Core fault is not shown to lower to a fault.
assumptions: moduleA m = true. It is decidable and checked on the goldens (Goose/Lower/Witness.lean). The interpreter takes the type of an integer operation from its operand, as Core does, so the theorem needs no typing hypothesis in the fragment.
witnesses: Seven goldens satisfy moduleA (gir_straight, gir_div_zero, gir_div_overflow, gir_slice_oob, gir_int_overflow_debug, gir_cast_range_debug, gir_rebind_later_same_scope); four are checked to agree in Goose/Lower/Witness.lean. test/gir/golden/mutation.sh: moving the snapshot of an indexed view after its index expression is caught by agree.

label: deferred
limits: The rest of core-pilot: calls, return, if/while/for statements, short-circuit, if-expressions, block expressions, assert, abort, exit. Their lowering spans several blocks and needs a statement of what the final block table holds for the blocks one fragment creates, a fuel-monotonicity result for the interpreter and an induction on Core's fuel through calls. A for-each over an array that is read through a reference also needs Core's type safety, since the lowering chooses to reread the length from the static type of the owner. Faults are not covered.

label: model-proved
statement: validate m = ok implies, for every function: each block has exactly one terminator and it is last; every defining instruction is typed by Op.resultTy from the types of its operands and the recorded type is that type; every instruction that can abort or stands for a statement carries an origin; each implementation's summary contains the effects the provenance analysis finds. For constants, integer arithmetic, comparison, boolean negation and conversion, running on a frame whose operand cells hold the derived types finishes or aborts at an origin and never faults.
differs_from_target: Dominance and scope balance are not proved to follow from acceptance: both checks run iterative analyses (dominator sets, the scopes entered at each block) and their soundness is not argued. Typing is semantic only for the scalar operations above; memory, call and view operations are not. Reference lifetime is not implied: test/gir/invalid/gir_accepted_dangling_reference.json is accepted and its run faults with dangling_root. Summary closure is relative to the validator's own analysis.
assumptions: None beyond validate m = ok; the scalar theorem assumes the operand cells have the derived types.
witnesses: 38 modules in test/gir/invalid, each failing at the check its name gives, one accepted and faulting
